facts.business: Dhanlaxmi Cotex Limited is engaged in trading of securities, fabrics, and yarn.
key_risks: Market Risk: Investments in quoted securities exposed to fluctuations in market prices due to global economic conditions, interest rates, corporate earnings, geopolitical developments and investor sentiment.
Liquidity Risk: Mismatch between financial assets and liabilities and funds deployed in investments and trading activities.
Credit Risk: Customer credit exposure in fabrics and yarn trading business.
Inventory Risk: Fluctuation in cotton, yarn or fabric prices resulting in inventory valuation risks and impact on margins.
Interest Rate Risk: Changes in interest rates affecting borrowing costs, liquidity and investment returns.
Foreign Exchange Risk: Fluctuations in exchange rates affecting cost and profitability of import/export transactions.
Regulatory Risk: Changes in regulatory requirements affecting securities and textile-related activities.
Macroeconomic Risk: Performance influenced by domestic economic growth, inflation, commodity prices, monetary policy, international trade policies and geopolitical developments.
Volatility in Raw Material Prices: Fluctuations in prices of cotton, yarn, fibres, dyes, chemicals and other inputs affecting production costs and profit margins.
Dependence on Cotton and Agricultural Factors: Cotton production exposed to weather conditions, monsoon variability, pest attacks, crop yields and global price changes.
Global Trade and Tariff Risks: Changes in tariffs, trade agreements, import restrictions and non-tariff barriers in key export markets.
Intense International Competition: Competition from China, Bangladesh, Vietnam, Pakistan with lower manufacturing costs and preferential trade arrangements.
Demand and Market Volatility: Textile demand influenced by consumer spending, economic growth, fashion trends, inventory levels and purchasing decisions of large brands.
Energy, Labour and Operating Costs: Increases in electricity, fuel, wages, transportation, financing and other operating costs placing pressure on margins.
Fragmented Industry Structure and Technology Gaps: Limited access to modern technology, automation, scale efficiencies and advanced manufacturing processes.
Supply Chain and Logistics Risks: Disruptions in availability or transportation of inputs, geopolitical tensions, shipping disruptions and freight cost changes.
Import Competition: Increasing imports from lower-cost manufacturing countries creating pricing pressure for domestic manufacturers.
Regulatory and Policy Risks: Changes in government policies relating to taxation, import duties, export incentives, labour regulations, environmental standards and trade policies.
